items.title: 34. Describe a piece of local news that people are interested in

questions.question: Describe a piece of local news that people are interested in
cue_card: What it was about
Where you saw/heard it
Who was involved
And explain why people were interested in it

answers.label: Part 2 Sample Answer
answers.english: I’m going to describe local news that was interesting to me. The weather of my locality has been experiencing serious turbulence these days, which is only about a week ahead of the summer holiday. It has been raining for the past few days which has intruded on our ordinary life to a great extent. Therefore, when I watched the daily weather forecast on TV informing that the weather would be okay in the next month, with sunlight and warmth, I felt great joy inside me. (When you got this news) Actually, the rainy season has become one of the specialties of my ancient city. Due to the foul weather and heavy rain, life in the city has been standing still. It has been immensely uncomfortable for most residents to go out and even work in such heavy showers. Yesterday, while I was having dinner with my family, we felt a sense of relief to hear on the local channel about the beautiful weather of our city during this summer holiday, because we were planning on a summer vacation. The rainy season last summer fell short of our expectations, so I really expected a balmy summer this year. (And explain why the local news was interesting to you) The most important thing is that if the weather is stable and nice as described, people in my city will be able to enjoy their summer holiday to the fullest. Amid the unfavorable weather, everybody seems to be sluggish and demotivated. To be honest, the thought of being forced to repeat tasks in the rain virtually exhausts me and I’m really scared that the situation would ruin my precious days off of the year. So, when the information was officially revealed, I became cheerful. I plan to do a lot of activities during this long break in an upbeat mood.

questions.question: How do people usually get local news nowadays?

answers.label: Part 3 Answer
answers.english: Most people get local news through their phones — Facebook, news apps, online portals, and increasingly TikTok. Traditional outlets like TV and newspapers are losing ground, especially among younger audiences. There's also a rise of community group chats on Zalo or Facebook, where neighbors share information about local events, scams, or traffic. It's faster and more personal than mainstream media.

questions.question: Do you think local news is more important than international news? Why?

answers.label: Part 3 Answer
answers.english: It depends on context. Local news is more immediately relevant — it affects your daily commute, weather, neighborhood events, or local policies. However, international news shapes the broader world we live in, including the economy and global trends. Ideally, people should follow both, but they often have different priorities at different stages of life.

questions.question: Why are some news stories more popular than others?

answers.label: Part 3 Answer
answers.english: Popular stories usually tap into strong emotions — outrage, sympathy, curiosity, or humor. Stories involving celebrities, scandals, or dramatic events get clicks. Algorithms on social media also amplify content that gets engagement, creating a feedback loop. Unfortunately, this means serious but "boring" news often gets overlooked while sensational stories dominate the feed.

People also tend to scroll headlines rather than read full articles, leading to a more superficial understanding of issues.

cue_card: What it was
When and where you had this problem
How the problem was solved
And explain how you felt when you had this problem

answers.label: Part 2 Sample Answer
answers.english: I’m going to talk about virtual communication tools like SKYPE. Skype is a telecommunications application software product that specializes in providing video chat and voice calls between computers, tablets, mobile devices, and smartwatches via the Internet. It is very user-friendly and anyone can soon master it if they have some basic computer literacy. (how did you learn about it?) This app was applied in my English online class. With the spread of English in recent years, I think it is a must to be able to use English fluently, but I live in the countryside, which doesn’t have any English class, and I can’t commute to the city centre every week due to my busy schedule. Finally I can solve my problem by using Skype and attend an English class with no need to travel from my place. Online learning through Skype and other telecommunication apps is a new wave in our education environment, and it has made many educational courses and a wealth of material accessible to anyone in the world. (how often do you use it?) This app has supported face-to-face communication and encouraged interactive learning between students and teachers. At first, I used Skype to attend my class twice a week and have a personal meeting with my tutor once a week. But then I made friends with some foreigners via Skype, so I can put the knowledge gained into practice by talking with them. Therefore, I use this app way more often. I even have some video conferences with my colleagues, which helps me a lot in my work. (and explain what differences it brings to your life) As I said already, I use Skype for studying and now in my work as well. This app makes a significant contribution to my life. It gives me opportunities to learn and to interact with other people, and helps me to save a lot of time.

questions.question: What kinds of technological problems do people often face?

answers.label: Part 3 Answer
answers.english: The most common ones are slow internet, software crashes, and forgotten passwords. Beyond that, people deal with phones running out of battery at critical moments, app updates that break features they relied on, and compatibility issues between devices. For older users, just navigating new interfaces and confusing menus can be a major hurdle.

answers.label: Part 3 Answer
answers.english: Tremendously. questions.question: What should people do when technology fails?

answers.label: Part 3 Answer
answers.english: Stay calm and have fallback options. Keeping a paper notebook for important contacts, knowing basic directions without GPS, and saving offline copies of critical documents all help. It's also smart to know basic troubleshooting — restarting devices, checking connections, contacting support. Above all, being patient is key; tech problems are often temporary inconveniences rather than disasters.

answers.label: Part 3 Answer
answers.english: I'm cautiously optimistic. AI and machine learning should help systems self-diagnose and fix problems automatically. So while individual issues may decrease, the interconnected nature of modern tech means that when something fails, it can affect many things at once.

questions.question: Describe a time when you had to get up very early
cue_card: Where you were
What time you had to get up
Why you had to get up so early
And explain how you felt about getting up very early

answers.label: Part 2 Sample Answer
answers.english: Actually, I’m a morning bird, so I found it quite easy to get up early. Fresh air and a great sense of tranquility in the morning made me feel invigorated, optimistic and creative, so I could concentrate more on my study. Well, it was last semester when the important final exam approached, and there were so many demanding subjects to handle.. Therefore, I decided to get up earlier than usual in the morning to prepare for the exam for the last week. (What you needed to do that day) It was quite discomforting at that time, as I had to wake exactly at 3 or 4 am to cram all the books. Mornings, for me at least, are the most productive time of day to study. I like to do some reading and memorizing in the morning, when there are no distractions. Looking back, I think I did take advantage of all that extra time. (And explain how you felt about getting up early) Actually, during that stressful week, I was totally exhausted and even suffered a headache. My brain was burdened with numerous subjects such as Maths, History, Literature and so on. Memorizing historic dates or Maths formulas in just a week requires a lot of persistence and determination. I remember drinking coffee many times a day to keep me wide awake. It was simply a nightmare but fortunately, I passed the exam with flying colors.

questions.question: Do young people and older people have different sleeping habits?

answers.label: Part 3 Answer
answers.english: Absolutely. Young people, especially teenagers and university students, tend to be night owls — staying up late and sleeping in. Their biological clocks are naturally shifted later. Older people, by contrast, often wake up early without an alarm and go to bed sooner. This isn't just preference; it's partly due to changes in circadian rhythms as we age.

questions.question: Describe a home that you like to visit but did not want to live in
cue_card: Where it is
What it is like
What you visited it for
And explain why you would not like to live there

answers.label: Part 2 Sample Answer
answers.english: My older sister, Lan, who is married to a doctor, lives in a large apartment and this is quite an elegant apartment in my opinion. Therefore, I would like to talk about this apartment which is located in the centre of Ho Chi Minh City. (How often you go there) The apartment is on the third floor of a six-storied building. It is only 20 minutes' walking distance from my school. On average, I visit my sister and her husband twice a month. (What it is like) Originally, my sister and her husband had wanted to buy a house in the suburb but they changed their mind and settled down in the city centre. The apartment is comparatively spacious but it has a cosy atmosphere. The rooms all have attached bathrooms and most of the furniture was bought from the most renowned and branded shops. My sister had an interior design diploma and she has put every effort to make her own house look beautiful. From a neutral point of view, I would say she is a talented interior designer as she has been quite successful in making the interior of her own house impressive. The large wooden furniture, the modern and sophisticated design of most of the furniture and handpicked wall frames gives a rich impression to a guest who visits this apartment. (And explain how you feel about the home) I like this apartment because it has got a lot of space, unlike many other apartments I have visited. The rooms give complete privacy to the house members as they are not adjacent to each other. The interior of the apartment is quite attractive. Moreover, my sister, as an interior designer has designed it perfectly. The apartment gives me the impression of beauty and comfort. For these reasons, I love this apartment.

answers.label: Part 2 Sample Answer
answers.english: Childhood has its uniqueness and magic and sometimes childhood friends are unforgettable. One such friend of mine was Minh who I still remember. Our friendship lasted only for a year and after that, he moved to a different city with his parents. (Where you met each other) Our first encounter took place on the very first day of secondary school. I was late for school due to bad traffic and I thought that all of the seats in the classroom were occupied. Thankfully, Miss Loan, my new teacher asked my name and gave me a hand. Then, one of the boys was asking me to go over and sit beside him. That boy was Minh. (What you often did together) At lunchtime, I shared my food with him and talked about lots of things. From that time onwards, we started sitting next to each other and our friendship began to flourish. I also found out that we had many hobbies in common. At school, we were on the same football and volleyball team. In the afternoon, we made kites and flew them together near the riverbank. Furthermore, as amateur collectors, our pastime was to spend hours looking for unique stamps in the library. We became very close friends but after one year I heard that he would be moving to Da Nang as his father had been transferred there. Since then, I have lost touch with him. (And explain what made you like him/her) Although I no longer catch up with him, he has always been the treasure of my childhood. Minh is a kind-hearted and open-minded person, so he really made that one year a delightful period for me. I really hope one day, I can contact him and keep our friendship forever.

What made you change the plan

And how you felt about the change

answers.label: Part 2 Sample Answer
answers.english: I'd like to talk about a recent travel plan that I had to completely revamp at the last minute — a trip to Da Nang I'd been planning for months with three of my best friends. We had everything sorted: flights booked, hotel reserved, an itinerary packed with beach days, motorbike rides up the Hai Van Pass, and food tours through the night markets. We'd been counting down for weeks. Then, just two days before departure, one of my friends came down with a bad case of flu, and another had a sudden family emergency. We were down from four to two overnight. After a long video call, the two of us decided not to cancel altogether but to pivot to something quieter. We swapped the beach holiday for a road trip up to Da Lat — a cool, peaceful mountain town only six hours from where we live. We canceled the flights, refunded most of our bookings, and hit the road instead. It was a complete change in vibe and pace. Honestly, I was disappointed at first — we'd dreamed about Da Nang for ages. But the Da Lat trip turned out to be unexpectedly wonderful. Just two of us in a quiet town meant deeper conversations, slower mornings with coffee overlooking pine forests, and a much-needed break from the noise of city life. Looking back, I'm grateful things didn't go as planned. Sometimes the detours in life lead to the most memorable moments.

I began to notice serious downsides — I felt isolated, my creativity took a hit, and I missed those spontaneous chats with colleagues that often led to the best ideas. answers.english: I'm going to talk about a small local history museum I visited in my hometown last summer. It had been around for decades but rarely attracted any visitors, and I went there mainly out of curiosity, since my grandmother had mentioned it many times as a place she used to enjoy. I went alone on a Saturday afternoon, hoping to spend a quiet hour learning something new about the area. To put it bluntly, the experience was mind-numbingly dull. The museum was filled with outdated displays — yellowing photographs, dusty glass cases, and tiny labels you could barely read. There were no interactive elements, no videos, no audio guides. I think the main reason it felt boring was the lack of engagement. Modern museums are usually designed to immerse visitors through storytelling and hands-on activities. This one, however, seemed stuck in time — relying purely on static exhibits that demand a lot of patience and prior interest. The lighting was dim, the temperature was uncomfortably warm, and there wasn't a single other visitor in sight, which made the whole place feel a bit eerie. Looking back, I don't entirely regret going. It made me appreciate just how much effort modern museums put into making history come alive. But I wouldn't go back unless they did a serious renovation.

It was my decision regarding what to study in university: whether to pursue my childhood dream of fine art or to stick with English which is my strength. (When you made your decision) As high school students, we all had to decide what we wanted for our life at some point during those years. Some people were at a loss, luckily I was not one of them as I already knew what I wanted and what my strength was. However, they weren’t the same and thus my problem started there. (How long it took to make the decision) I didn’t really think about it in my first year of high school, but the problem became clearer and clearer afterwards. And it was not until my final semester in high school was I able to make up my mind that I’d go with English. So, I’d say I spent two years thinking about it. I was torn between my dream and the reality before my eyes: fine art was what I had always wanted to do, but there wasn’t much place for it in the market as far as I know, and the competition was intense; while English was not quite what I dreamed of, but it was more realistic and easier to get a job. I ended up studying English to make a living and chose to let art stay by my side as my ultimate hobby. I have no regrets regarding my choice, at least until now.

answers.label: Part 2 Sample Answer

The story revolves around a young lion cub named Simba who is the heir to the throne of the Pride Lands. After his evil uncle Scar orchestrates the death of Simba's father, Mufasa, Simba runs away in shame, believing he caused the tragedy. He grows up in the jungle with two unlikely friends — a meerkat named Timon and a warthog named Pumbaa — until he eventually returns home to reclaim his rightful place and restore harmony to the kingdom. Apart from the lions, the film features a whole cast of animals — wise baboons, scheming hyenas, colorful birds, even singing insects. The African savanna feels alive with personality, and each animal has its own quirks that make them memorable. Watching it again as an adult, I was struck by how emotionally layered the story is. On the surface, it's a colorful adventure for kids, but beneath that, it's a profound tale about grief, guilt, responsibility, and the circle of life. The scene where Mufasa dies still hits hard, and Simba's journey of self-discovery resonates with anyone who's ever had to face their past. The visuals were breathtaking, the music timeless, and I left the cinema feeling both nostalgic and inspired. It's the kind of story that stands the test of time.

answers.label: Part 2 Sample Answer
answers.english: I'd like to talk about an old friend of mine from high school named Linh, who went silent on me for nearly three months last year. We used to be quite close — same circle of friends, always studying together. After graduation she moved abroad for university, and we still kept in touch through Messenger from time to time. Around the start of last year, I sent her a long message catching up on life, sharing some big news about my new job, and asking how she was settling into her new city. I genuinely expected a reply within a day or two. But days turned into weeks, and there was no response. At first I assumed she was busy with exams, then I started wondering if I'd said something wrong. It nagged at me for weeks. I considered double-texting but didn't want to seem needy or annoying. The silence felt oddly hurtful, even though I knew she probably didn't mean anything by it. She finally replied about three months later with a heartfelt apology, explaining she had been going through a tough time — homesick, depressed, and overwhelmed by university life. She admitted she'd opened my message but couldn't muster the energy to respond. Honestly, hearing that melted my frustration away. I felt sorry for her rather than annoyed, and we're back to chatting regularly now. The whole experience taught me not to take delayed replies personally.

(What do you usually do to celebrate?) During Tet, my family and I engage in a number of customs and traditions to mark this auspicious occasion. To kick things off, we usually roll up our sleeves and embark on a deep cleaning of our house, symbolizing the act of clearing out the old year's bad luck and welcoming fresh and positive energies for the upcoming year. We also prepare traditional dishes like banh chung and pay a visit to our ancestors' graves to pay our respects. One of my favorite traditions is giving and receiving lucky red envelopes (called "li xi" in Vietnamese) filled with money, which symbolizes good luck and prosperity for the year ahead. (Who do you usually celebrate with?) Tet is a time for family reunions, so I usually celebrate it with my extended family, including grandparents, aunts, uncles, and cousins. We gather under one roof for a grand feast, which is a moment of joy. We exchange stories, laughter, and reminisce about the good old days. (And explain why you enjoy it) What makes Tet so enjoyable for me is the feeling of renewal that it brings. It's a time when we turn over a new leaf, leaving behind any past grievances and focusing on the future with optimism. The vibrant decorations, the delicious traditional foods, and the laughter of family members create an atmosphere that warms my heart.

Honestly, this doesn’t take up much time but it can save a great amount of effort from going down the drain in a computer breakdown like this.

answers.label: Part 2 Sample Answer
answers.english: (What the product is) The first thing that springs to my mind when I go to Hanoi, the capital of Vietnam, is cốm. This is a seasonal dish associated with autumn and is a popular seasonal dessert across Vietnam, especially in Red River Delta cuisine. I first heard of this traditional product in a Vietnamese poem when I was in grade 8. It is described as pearls from God because of its tastiness and beauty. (When did you try this product for the first time) I got to try cốm for the first time on my trip to Hanoi in 2016, just one year after I knew the poem. The poet exactly described cốm, from its flavour to its texture and taste. The taste is slightly sweet with a nutty flavour. It can be eaten plain or with coconut shavings. At first, I was afraid that cốm would fall short of my expectations as poets often exaggerated the tastiness of the food. But I was really overwhelmed by this traditional food. (What it is made of) Cốm, commonly known as green rice, is basically a flattened rice dish in Vietnamese cuisine. It is not dyed green, as can be done with pandan, but is immature rice kernels roasted over very low heat and then pounded in a mortar and pestle until flattened. It is wrapped in lotus leaves instead of plastic, which gives it an even better flavour. (And explain how you feel about it) I think this type of food is underestimated by foreign tourists and even Vietnamese people. My friends always say that the food tastes too plain. I think it is because they’re used to eating food with strong flavours and spices. Cốm is pretty natural, which makes it quite special in today’s world. So, I believe that it should be valued more by both Vietnamese and foreign tourists.

(What it is made of) Cốm, commonly known as green rice, is basically a flattened rice dish in Vietnamese cuisine. It is not dyed green, as can be done with pandan, but is immature rice kernels roasted over very low heat and then pounded in a mortar and pestle until flattened. It is wrapped in lotus leaves instead of plastic, which gives it an even better flavour.

(And explain how you feel about it) I think this type of food is underestimated by foreign tourists and even Vietnamese people. My friends always say that the food tastes too plain. I think it is because they’re used to eating food with strong flavours and spices. Cốm is pretty natural, which makes it quite special in today’s world. So, I believe that it should be valued more by both Vietnamese and foreign tourists.

items.topic: 61. Describe a time when you changed a decision
items.title: 61. Describe a time when you changed a decision

questions.question: Describe a time when you changed a decision
cue_card: What decision you made
Why you changed the decision
Is it a good result
And explain how you felt about it

answers.label: Part 2 Sample Answer
answers.english: I'd like to talk about the time I changed my decision about studying abroad — possibly one of the most important U-turns I've ever made. After graduating from high school, I had set my heart on going to Australia for university. I'd done all the research, taken IELTS, applied to several schools, and even received an offer from a decent university in Melbourne. My family was supportive and the plan seemed solid. However, about two months before departure, I had a long conversation with my father about finances. He didn't say it directly, but I could tell the cost would put serious strain on the family budget. On top of that, I started having doubts about whether I was emotionally ready to live alone on the other side of the world. After several sleepless nights, I made the gut-wrenching decision to stay and study at a local university instead. Looking back, it turned out to be a blessing in disguise. The local university I chose had an excellent program, I made wonderful friends, and I was able to take on internships that kickstarted my career early. Financially, my family didn't have to stretch themselves thin, and I graduated with no debt. At the time, the decision felt devastating, but now I'm convinced it was the right call. It taught me that sometimes the path you didn't take is the one that leads you to a better destination.

questions.question: Why do some people find it difficult to make important decisions?

answers.label: Part 3 Answer
answers.english: Big decisions often come with high stakes and uncertain outcomes, which naturally creates anxiety. Some people are perfectionists who fear making the wrong choice, while others struggle with decision fatigue — they're overwhelmed by too many options. Lack of confidence, fear of regret, and pressure from family or society can also paralyze a person when making important calls.

questions.question: Do young people make decisions differently from older people?

answers.label: Part 3 Answer
answers.english: Yes, quite differently. Young people tend to be more impulsive and willing to take risks — they have less to lose and time on their side. Older people, by contrast, usually weigh things more carefully, drawing on past experience and considering long-term consequences. Neither approach is inherently better; they suit different stages of life.

questions.question: Who do people usually ask for advice when making important decisions?

answers.english: Most commonly, people turn to those they trust deeply — family members, especially parents, and close friends. For career-related decisions, mentors and senior colleagues are often consulted. Some also seek objective opinions from professionals like financial advisors or counselors, who can offer expertise without emotional bias.

questions.question: Do you think people should always think carefully before making decisions?

answers.english: For major decisions, absolutely. Rushing into things can lead to regret. However, overthinking small choices wastes mental energy. The trick is matching the level of deliberation to the importance of the decision. For trivial matters, going with your gut is often fine; for life-changing ones, careful analysis is essential.

questions.question: Can difficult decisions help people grow as individuals? Why?

answers.label: Part 3 Answer
answers.english: Without a doubt. Difficult decisions force us to clarify our values, weigh trade-offs, and take responsibility for our lives. They build resilience and self-awareness. Even when the outcome isn't ideal, the process of making the decision teaches us about ourselves. People who avoid hard choices often remain stuck in their comfort zone.

questions.question: Describe a special cake you received from others
cue_card: When it happened
Where it happened
Who you got the cake from
And explain why it's a special cake

answers.label: Part 2 Sample Answer
answers.english: (When it happened) Last year, I went on a Da Lat trip with my ex-boyfriend to Da Lat, which is one of the most popular mountain retreats for those residing in Ho Chi Minh City. It just so happened that I stayed at a local 5-star resort right on my birthday. It is one of the best birthdays I’d ever had in my life. (Where it happened) When the front desk agent checked me and my boyfriend in, she greeted us and requested to scan my ID Card. The front desk agent could have probably seen my birthday then and told other staff to get a birthday cake for me. Upon arrival at my room, I saw a well-prepared birthday cake and some other birthday decorations like balloons. (Who you got the cake from) Honestly, I totally didn’t expect such a surprise birthday cake from this resort. It was also my first stay there, not a loyal member. Then, I realised that my ex was a loyal member of the resort so he made use of his membership privileges to get the cake for me. (And explain why it’s a special cake) When I ate the first slice of the cake, I quickly realised it was unsweetened! I was like: “Really, babe?” and at a loss for words before recalling that my ex was allergic to sugar. That was the first, and probably the last, unsweetened cake I’d ever eaten in my life. It was so disgusting that I couldn’t eat another slice. Sadly, just some months after that very trip, we broke up. But I was truly happy that he and the hotel staff team made my 22nd birthday so memorable.

questions.question: What are the differences between the special food in Vietnam and foreign countries?

answers.label: Part 3 Answer
answers.english: Vietnamese delicacies have the uniqueness that cannot be found anywhere else. It is full of natural spices, like cinnamon, cloves, and various kinds of herbs. Also, Vietnamese foods are pretty healthy as they are high in fiber thanks to the use of many different types of vegetables. Vietnamese foods are pretty much soup-based such as pho, beef noodles, while food from other countries tends to be used without broth.

questions.question: Do people usually cook special food in Vietnam?

Besides, we also cook special food on special occasions like birthdays or traditional feasts or festivals.
